title: Intraday anomaly correlator for high-cardinality usage signals
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Goal: Build a low-noise, intraday anomaly correlator service that detects and groups anomalies across usage, cost, and latency signals at high cardinality (customer, route, model) and surfaces actionable alerts to Console and on-call.
description_details: Motivation: existing daily batch detectors miss short-lived spikes and create delayed incident responses. We need an intraday pipeline (multi-minute latency) that complements nightly models and reduces mean time to detection for customer-impacting billing/latency issues. Scope: streaming input from metric-ingest (Kafka), lightweight stateful baselining per key, adaptive thresholds, cross-metric correlation (e.g., p95 latency + token rate + model fallback rate), deduping/grouping, and alert routing with severity tiers. Non-goals: full ML model training (XGBoost/NN) in first iteration; we will start with robust statistical detectors and heuristics with a pluggable ML stage later.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Detect intraday anomalies within 10 minutes of onset for 80% of synthetic injection tests across a range of customers and routes. 2) Reduce actionable false positive alerts (pager + Slack) by 50% relative to current naive thresholding for the pilot group. 3) Group correlated anomalies so a single incident covers related metric spikes. 4) Expose detection events to Console (alerts view) and to the existing incident webhook for on-call routing. 5) Monitor precision/recall and alert fatigue metrics via new dashboard.
design_decisions: - Use streaming processor (Flink/Materialize prototype) reading metric topics; maintain per-key windows for baseline computation (EWMA + seasonal adjustment for intraday profiles). - Adaptive thresholds: combine multiplicative deviation from baseline with quantile-based outlier scoring to handle heavy tails. - Correlation step: build a windowed join across metric types, rank candidate signals by joint anomaly score, and emit grouped incidents. - High-cardinality strategy: sample low-traffic keys for full state, use sketch summaries (tDigest) for very high-cardinality groups, and materialize hotspots to ClickHouse for backfill + inspection. - Alert dedupe: cluster events by (customer, route prefix, model_family) and collapse duplicates within 30 minutes. - Storage: anomaly events go to events-store (ClickHouse) and a short-lived Redis cache for rapid dedupe queries. - Rollout: pilot on 5 customers (including one enterprise and two high-volume PLG accounts) with opt-in toggle in Console.
implementation_notes: - Input schema: {timestamp, customer_id, route, model, metric_name, metric_value, tags}. Use existing ingestion topic names: metrics.events.v2 and metrics.summary.v2. - Compute p95/p99 where possible from precomputed summaries; fall back to raw aggregates for sampled routes. - Use feature flags to toggle correlation and grouping separately from detection so we can A/B test grouping heuristics. - Add tracing to the pipeline (X-Request-ID propagation) to assist RCA when alerts are noisy. - Ensure cost budget: estimate 2 additional Flink task slots + ClickHouse storage ~150 GB for 90-day retention for anomaly events in pilot.
risks_and_mitigation: - Risk: high-cardinality state may blow up memory. Mitigation: enforce per-customer state caps, evict LRU keys, and aggregate low-volume routes into 'other' buckets. - Risk: noisy alerts causing pager fatigue. Mitigation: conservative initial thresholds, hold for 2 consecutive window ticks before paging, route initial alerts to #telemetry-signalops Slack channel for triage. - Risk: regressions in billing metrics from false positives. Mitigation: run synthetic injection tests simulating token spikes and cost increases; require human sign-off before paging any customer-facing incident.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (week 1-2): deploy detectors in read-only mode emitting to internal dashboard only. Phase 2 (week 3): enable Slack notifications for pilot customers (no paging). Phase 3 (week 4): enable paging for critical-severity anomalies for pilot customers. Phase 4 (week 6): expand to 25% of accounts and start decay tuning. Each phase includes 48-hour observation windows and rollback gates. Use feature flag console.telemetry.anomaly.pilot to control enrollment.
metrics_to_track: - Detection latency (minutes) - Alert precision and recall (weekly) - Pager rate per 1k customers - Alert-to-incident conversion rate - Average anomaly group size (number of metrics merged) - Storage and processing cost delta compared to baseline
test_plan: - Unit tests for baseline and threshold math. - Integration tests with local Flink/Materialize harness using recorded metric dump. - Synthetic injection suite: run 50+ scenarios across traffic patterns (gradual drift, sudden spike, bursty noise) and assert detection within SLA. - Pilot validation: collect labeled alerts for two weeks and compute precision/recall against manual triage.
notes: Design reviewed with PM (Lena Ortiz) and Observability lead (Samir Patel) 2026-03-12. Observability suggested adding sampling logs for false positive investigations — added lightweight event debugger to write samples to S3. Security reviewed data retention and approved for pilot with standard PII masking.
